prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: individual Bible Journey illustration of two connected instructions in Galatians 6:1–2, landscape 1536×1024, full frame, no interface or text.
Input images: Image 1 and Image 2 are approved style references only. Match their warm cinematic realism, natural proportions, tactile materials, nuanced light, and respectful storytelling. Do not reproduce their scenes, characters, or compositions.
Scene/backdrop: One unlocated symbolic moment illustrating gentle restoration and bearing one another’s burdens. This is not a documented event or a claimed historical journey.
Subject/action: Show two fully clothed ordinary people helping one another in a quiet open setting. One carries a heavy woven bundle, and the other approaches gently, offers a steadying hand, and helps take some of the load. Their expressions are calm and respectful, with no humiliation, injury, or blame. The shared bundle is a visual metaphor for the burden Paul names, not an object from a specific event.
Composition/framing: Medium-wide view from several paces away; do not fill the frame vertically. Show both figures from head to lower leg, smaller within the scene, with their heads beginning below the 15% line and feet ending above the 88% line. Keep the shared bundle and helpful hand readable. Place the pair entirely within the left 60%; reserve the right 30% as quiet, low-detail ground and soft background for a reading panel. Leave open air above the heads and ground below the feet. One continuous interaction.
Style/materials: Warm realistic historical illustration; simple period-evocative woven garments without assigning identities, natural hands and faces, tactile cloth and basket weave, soft golden natural light, subdued earth pigments.
Constraints: Do not imply a particular fault, disability, route, or historical location. No text, labels, symbols, map, spectacle, modern items, pins, logos, border, or watermark.
notes: Final raster reviewed against the named subjects; account-specific references remain in the scene registry. Historical appearances are reconstructed and literary scenes are labeled.
